issues.display_title: Issue #627: Issue: Cannot Continue Creating a Project After Adding a Floor by Importing a MapThru Floor
Issue #680: Wizard Add More Floors: re-importing the same Mappedin ZIP stages duplicate level ids
issues.main_description_html:
Importing the same Mappedin ZIP twice through wizard step 2's Add More Floors stages two levels with the same level_id and two floor configs with the same id.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

  1. Wizard step 2 → import a Mappedin ZIP → review modal → Add More Floors
  2. Import the same ZIP again → Add More Floors
  3. The project now holds each imported level twice under the same id

Two ZIPs from different venues do not collide — Mappedin ids are venue-scoped — so this needs the same file (or two exports of the same venue) to bite.

Where

src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:196-210 merges into the live store while asking the merge to keep the file's ids:

const staged = mergeImportIntoProject({
  groups,
  levels: importSource.canvasData.levels,
  canvasData: store.canvasData,     // ← already holds the first import
  floorConfigs: store.floorConfigs,
  keepIds: true,
  prepend: true,
});

src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts:87 takes it at its word, with no check against what is already there:

const levelId = keepIds ? floor.id : newId();

The keepIds doc comment (mergeIntoProject.ts:22-27) justifies itself with "the import IS the project: nothing can collide". That holds for Continue to Editor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:146-152 passes canvasData: { ...src.canvasData, levels: [] } and floorConfigs: [] — an empty target) and does not hold for Add More Floors.

The obvious fix is wrong

Dropping keepIds from the Add More Floors call alone breaks the Uploaded list. handleRemoveImportedFloor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:237-249) unstages by the id the UI holds:

setFloorConfigs(store.floorConfigs.filter((f) => f.id !== id));
if (base) setCanvasData({ ...base, levels: base.levels.filter((l) => l.level_id !== id) });

and the ids the UI holds come from importedGroups, which is built from groupFloorsByBuilding(importResult) — i.e. the file's floor ids. Mint new ids in the merge and the remove button silently stops removing anything, because store ids no longer match the ones the list is keyed by.

So keepIds: true on this path is load-bearing, not an oversight. Whatever the fix is, the Uploaded list and the store have to end up agreeing on one set of ids.

Two shapes that would work

Pick whichever is smaller once you are in the code — both are fine, this is not a decision that needs making up front:

  1. Collide-aware ids in the merge. When keepIds is on, fall back to a fresh id for any floor whose id already exists in the target, and return the id mapping so the caller can restamp importedGroups. Keeps the UI keyed by whatever actually landed.
  2. Stage first, then derive the list. Let the merge always mint ids for this path and rebuild importedGroups from staged.floorConfigs instead of from importResult, so the list is downstream of the store rather than parallel to it.

Not in scope: Continue to Editor's keepIds (its target is empty by construction), and the information/category staging below it — Information carries no level id, and those records are already de-duplicated by their own id at StepUploadFloor.tsx:216-228.

Acceptance

  • Importing the same ZIP twice via Add More Floors produces distinct level_ids and distinct floorConfig.ids
  • Both copies appear in the Uploaded list, and removing one removes exactly that one from the list and from the store
  • Continue to Editor is unchanged — imported ids still match the staged Information records
  • Existing uploads and previously imported floors are untouched
  • A case in src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/mergeIntoProject.test.ts covers merging a group whose ids already exist in the target
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Found while validating PRD #633 against the code — the grouping feature itself is already shipped (#643 → #662), this is the one real defect the audit turned up.

RESULT

Branch: feature/680-import-duplicate-level-ids (from development) · Commit: dbfa496

Fix

keepIds is now a preference, not a promise. A floor whose id is already taken in the target gets a fresh one:

const levelId = keepIds && !taken.has(floor.id) ? floor.id : newId();
taken.add(levelId);
idMap.set(floor.id, levelId);

taken is seeded from the target's level ids and its floor config ids — configs are keyed by level id, so a duplicate there breaks the floor list just as badly — and grows as the merge hands ids out, so a file that lists the same floor twice cannot collide with itself either.

Continue to Editor is unaffected. Its target is empty by construction (canvasData: { ...src.canvasData, levels: [] }, floorConfigs: []), so every id it asks for is free and the review modal still predicts the project exactly. Covered by a regression test.

Why not just drop keepIds at the call site

That was the smaller diff and the wrong one. importedGroups — the Uploaded list — is built from the import, and handleRemoveImportedFloor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:237-249) filters the store by the ids that list holds. Minting ids the list never learns about leaves a remove button that quietly removes nothing.

So the merge reports where each floor landed, and the caller restamps:

setImportedGroups((prev) => [
  ...groups.map((g) => ({
    ...g,
    floors: g.floors.map((f) => ({ ...f, id: staged.idMap.get(f.id) ?? f.id })),
  })),
  ...prev,
]);

The setImportedGroups call also moved to after the merge, since it now depends on its result.

Re-keying is safe

Checked before writing it: nothing persisted in canvasData references a level by id. level_id appears exactly once in useMapStore.types.ts (on LevelData itself); doors hang off wallId; Information links through area.infoId and carries no level id. Every other levelId in the codebase is ephemeral — collab presence, runtime params, snap matches. A re-keyed level takes nothing with it.

Files

 src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts             | +19 −4
 src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/mergeIntoProject.test.ts | +88
 src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx                | +14 −5

Checks

pnpm test 142 files, 1165 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed · pnpm lint clean · tsc --noEmit clean.

Baseline on clean development is 1161 passed, so the delta is exactly the four tests added.

Three of the four were confirmed to fail with the guard reverted:

  • mints a fresh id for an imported floor whose id the project already holds — FAILS without
  • reports where every imported floor landed — FAILS without
  • does not let one import collide with itself when a file lists a floor twice — FAILS without
  • still keeps the file's ids when the target is empty — passes either way by design; it is the regression guard for Continue to Editor

Not covered by automation

The acceptance item "removing one removes exactly that one from the list and from the store" is the reason for the idMap restamp, but there is no component test for StepUploadFloor — the file has none today and standing one up needs the whole wizard store plus file-picker plumbing. Worth one manual pass: import a ZIP → Add More Floors → import the same ZIP → remove one of the second copy's floors → confirm exactly that floor leaves both the Uploaded list and the staged project.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/680/video-680-duplicate-import-ids.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 71.8 s, recorded against a production build (pnpm build + the standalone server) in an isolated worktree, not next dev.

The scenario drives the real wizard: new project → Manual Coordinates on the fixture's venue → step 2 → import mappedin-two-buildings.zip → Add More Floors → import the same file again → Add More Floors.

It proves the fix without ever showing an id, because the id is what the Remove button filters by:

Moment Uploaded list
After the first import 3 floors across 2 buildings
After re-importing the same file 6 floors across 4 sections — same names, same buildings
After removing one floor 5 floors — only that row went, and its twin in the other copy is still there

Before this commit that last number was 4: both copies shared one id, so one click filtered both out of the staged project.

Every count is asserted inside the scenario, not just narrated — it throws if the screen disagrees, so a recording that completes is a passing test.

GPU path verified separately for this run: the angle+vulkan config record.sh uses reports ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312 (NVIDIA Tesla P4), NVIDIA). The libEGL /dev/dri/card1 warnings in the log come from the other probe configurations and are noise.

issues.display_title: Issue #684: Direction search: show the building name under each result, not the description
issues.main_description_html:
In the Direction panel's destination and origin search, the second line of each result should be the building's name.

Assigned to: @alfarez21

Reported in #653. Both screenshots are the same list, and the red underline marks the line that is wrong:

What it does today

One component renders both lists — src/components/editor/preview/DirectionAreaAutocomplete.tsx:113-118:

<span className="w-full truncate text-sm font-medium" ...>
  {title} · {option.levelName}
</span>
{showDescription && info.description && (
  <span className="mt-0.5 w-full truncate text-xs" ...>{info.description}</span>
)}

The two fields differ only in that flag:

Field Prop Second line today
TO (destination) showDescription — DirectionPanel.tsx:82 the Information record's description — "kelapa meeting", "ruang tester"
FROM (origin) showDescription={false} — DirectionPanel.tsx:124 nothing

That is exactly what the screenshots show: a wrong second line in the first, a missing one in the second.

What it should do

Second line = the building the area sits in, on both fields.

The building is one hop from data the option already carries. Options are built in src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:148-166, level by level, so the level record is in hand:

import { buildingOfLevel } from "@/lib/map/geojson-utils";
// per level, alongside levelId / levelName:
buildingName: buildingOfLevel(canvasData, level)?.name

DirectionAreaOption (DirectionAreaAutocomplete.tsx:8-12) gains that field and the row renders it instead of the description.

Reaches three surfaces at once

PreviewOverlay is the only consumer, and it is mounted by the editor's Preview mode, src/app/preview/[projectId]/page.tsx, and the public share src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx. One change, all three — worth checking all three, nothing extra to write.

Two things to decide while in there

  1. The description is being replaced, and it is searchable today. DirectionAreaAutocomplete.tsx:50 matches typed text against info.description, so a user can currently find a room by its description text. Dropping the line raises the question of whether that match should stay. Keeping the match while hiding the text is defensible (search finds more than it shows); so is dropping both. Pick one deliberately rather than by accident.

  2. Projects with no building records. buildingOfLevel returns undefined when canvasData.buildings is empty or missing (geojson-utils.ts:190-197) — every pre-buildings project is in that state. Either fall back to MAIN_BUILDING (geojson-utils.ts:929, the name used elsewhere for the implicit default) or render no second line at all. Do not print an empty row.

Acceptance

  • Destination results show the building name on the second line
  • Origin results show it too — they have no second line today
  • The name matches the building the area's level belongs to, including a level with no explicit buildingId (it belongs to the first building record)
  • A project with no building records renders cleanly — no blank second line
  • Point-annotation endpoints get the same treatment as areas; both come through the same option list
  • Editor Preview, /preview/[projectId] and /v/[key] all read the same
  • Search behaviour is whatever decision 1 settled on, and the decision is stated in the PR
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

There is no test file for DirectionAreaAutocomplete or DirectionPanel today. A small one covering the building-name line and the no-buildings fallback would be the first, and is worth adding — jsdom and @testing-library/react are already installed.

issues.display_title: Issue #675: Editor Map: a placement drag rebuilds the whole model every mousemove (917 ms/event)
issues.main_description_html:
Dragging a floor or a building on the Editor Map is not interactive. Every mousemove writes canvasData, and that write costs far more than a frame.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Measured

Production build (next build + the standalone server, not next dev), Selected Floor drag, ten mousemove events, wall-clock per event:

Project Objects Information records ms per mousemove
43fada28 144 219 917 ms
6397e363 4 37 202 ms

A 60 fps frame is 16.6 ms. The heavier project is 55× over budget, and the near-empty one is still 12× over. The cost scales with project size, so it gets worse exactly where it matters.

Dev builds are roughly 1.8× worse again (1649 ms and 556 ms) — worth knowing when reproducing, but the production numbers above are the ones to fix against.

Scripts: .playwright-mcp/demo/672/probe-dragcost.mjs (timing) and probe-profile.mjs (CPU profile).

Why

One setCanvasDataSilent per mousemove re-renders the whole editor subtree, and three separate consumers each do full work off it:

  1. The map rebuilds every level's geometry. useFloorPlanLayer lists canvasData in its dependency array (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts:198) and answers with canvasDataToGeoJson(...) + source.setData(...) (:195-197). That re-tessellates every wall of every rendered level into polygons, then MapLibre re-tiles and re-uploads the buffers. The profile shows bufferData and shader-program work inside the drag window.

  2. The 2D editor re-syncs even though it is not on screen. FloorplanEditor is mounted in Map mode and only visually hidden — EditorCanvas.tsx:48-49 wraps it in a hidden div and passes active={false} rather than unmounting it. detectRooms shows up in the drag profile as a result: room detection running because a floor was nudged three pixels on a map the editor is not displaying.

  3. Markers reposition. MapObjectMarkers' reposition pass appears in the same window.

None of this is what the gesture actually changed. A placement drag writes offsetX/offsetY on one level's mapTransform — the geometry is byte-identical before and after.

Not this

Two adjacent fixes already landed in #672 and neither touches this:

  • levelBBox now caches its result on the geometry object — that removed the snap's own per-move cost (7.344 ms → 0.049 ms), not the rebuild.
  • location is memoized, so an unrelated re-render no longer triggers a rebuild on its own. The rebuild still runs whenever canvasData genuinely changes, which during a drag is every event.

Directions

Not a decision, just where the cheap wins look like they are — worth measuring before committing to any of them:

  • Do not rebuild geometry for a placement-only change. A level's mapTransform is an affine transform; if it were applied at the layer level rather than baked into the GeoJSON, a drag would touch no vertices at all. Biggest win, biggest change.
  • Unmount the editor in Map mode, or make its sync bail when active is false. Cheapest of the three and independently correct — a hidden canvas should not be detecting rooms.
  • Coalesce the silent writes to one per animation frame. Bounds the damage without fixing the cause; useful if the two above turn out to be large.

Acceptance

  • A Selected Floor drag on the 144-object project costs well under one frame per mousemove, measured with probe-dragcost.mjs
  • Building-scope and All Buildings drags improve the same way — they take the same path
  • Geometry, room detection and marker positions are unchanged by a placement-only drag
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Found while recording the #672 demo: the recording ran at roughly one rendered frame per 1.6 s during drags, which is what sent me looking.

issues.display_title: Issue #690: Preview/live: rebuild the Search panel to the design/information-linking layout
issues.main_description_html:
The design/information-linking branch redesigned the preview/live Search panel. That layout was never integrated — it is the last un-ported piece of that branch.

#593 says it plainly: "the behaviour shipped, the layout did not. Only the visual layer was ported." Two waves followed — #586/#588 (Link to Information) and #587/#589 (visitor card + photo preview) — and neither touched search.

Evidence it is not in development

  • src/components/editor/preview/SearchAreaPanel.tsx on development is still the pre-design shape: a 280 px column of AreaAutocomplete with a separate bordered category card underneath.
  • The design's version (design/information-linking, f52cdb4) is a single 360 px aside panel with its own search field.
  • src/lib/information/{integration,policy,hours}.ts exist only on the design branch.

PRD #473's search behaviour is done and its issue is closed and labelled implemented — category browsing, title/description/keyword search, active-floor preference. This task is the layout only.

What differs, concretely

development today design branch
Container 280 px column, two separate blocks one 360 px aside, w-[min(360px,calc(100vw-2rem))], height bounded to the viewport
Search input AreaAutocomplete combobox, results in its own dropdown inline field in the panel header: search glyph, "Search places", clear button
Category list bordered card below the bar, FolderOpen + name + count "Browse by Category" heading, divided rows, min-h-12, name + count + chevron
Results inside the combobox dropdown rows in the panel body, min-h-14: title, floor badge, 2-line clamped description
Back out of a category chevron-left with the category name "← All Categories" link, and the heading becomes the category name
Empty states none "No places match "x"." / "No places are available in this category." / "No categories are available yet."
Typing filters per keystroke 250 ms debounce (INFORMATION_EXPERIENCE_POLICY.searchDebounceMs)
Small screens fixed 280 px width clamps to the viewport; text-base sm:text-sm so iOS does not zoom the field

Deliberately NOT ported

The design branch carries its own copies of logic development already has, and its versions are older:

  • distinctPreferredTargets — development has dedupeTargetsByInfo (src/lib/preview/searchTargets.ts), same active-floor rule, already tested, and PreviewOverlay already applies it before passing targets. Keep the existing one.
  • visibleCategories — the design's filters on membership alone; development computes the same set with the per-category counts the badge needs. Keep the existing one.
  • matchTargets is already exported from AreaAutocomplete on development — no change needed there, and AreaAutocomplete itself stays because DirectionPanel still uses it.

So this is a layout change plus one new constant, not a logic port.

Scope

  • src/components/editor/preview/SearchAreaPanel.tsx — rebuild to the design
  • src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx — only if the panel's wrapper/positioning needs it
  • One debounce constant, co-located rather than a new policy.ts
  • Tests: the pure parts (category visibility + counts, result matching incl. keywords, debounce behaviour) as vitest cases

Acceptance

  • Preview and live search render the design's single panel: header field, browse-by-category, results with floor badge and description
  • Clear button empties the query and returns to the category list
  • Entering a category shows its places; "All Categories" goes back; searching from inside a category searches everywhere
  • Every empty state has copy, none is a blank box
  • Typing is debounced at 250 ms
  • Category counts stay correct and empty categories stay hidden (PRD #473 R42/R43)
  • Search result activation still prefers a linked label on the current floor (#473 12.4) — dedupeTargetsByInfo still owns this
  • DirectionPanel is unaffected
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

issues.display_title: Issue #688: Editor Map: wall vertex edit mode — drag active-floor wall points, one undo per drag (PRD #681)
issues.main_description_html:
Map mode gets a wall edit toggle: turn it on and the active floor's wall points become draggable dots on the 3D map, so a multi-floor building can be lined up without bouncing between the 2D Editor and Map mode.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #681 (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-14-map-mode-wall-edit-tools/prd.md, branch product-docs) — R1–R14 and R19–R24. Snapping to the floor below is split out into #689.

None of this exists today: mapWallEditMode, wallVertexHandles, snapWallVertex, src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts and src/components/editor/map-wall-edit/ are all absent (grep is empty, files missing).

What is already in the repo — build on it, do not rewrite

Need Already here
DOM handles over MapLibre, reprojected on move/zoom/pitch src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx — the same overlay, already draggable via onMovePoint
Map position → active-floor model px lngLatToLevelPixel() src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:429; its doc comment says any consumer that WRITES a px position picked on the map must invert through this, not lngLatToPixel
Live drag without spamming undo setCanvasDataSilent src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:241, commit with history via setCanvasData :198 — exactly how the building drag already works (Editor3DMapView.tsx:240-241)
A press that must not start a pan, a building drag, or a selection markerHitRef screen-space hit list (Editor3DMapView.tsx:169,208,219, consumed at usePreviewSelectionLayers.ts:42) and hitsGuardLayer (useBuildingDrag.ts:45)
Building stack / active floor groupLevelsByBuilding() geojson-utils.ts:860 (levels per building, array order = bottom→top), scopedActiveLevelId in Editor3DMapView.tsx:98
No-walls state Editor3DMapView.tsx:360-372 already renders "This level has no walls to preview in 3D."

So nothing new is needed in the store beyond the mode flag. #681 §3 asks for a new live+commit wall action; movePoint (editorSlice.ts:463) is the closest precedent but it pushes no history entry at all — routing the drag through the existing silent/commit pair gives one undo entry per drag for free and keeps a single history code path.

Scope

  1. State — mapWallEditMode: boolean + setMapWallEditMode(on) in src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts. Ephemeral: not persisted, not part of canvasHistory, default false, forced off when leaving Map mode or unmounting Editor3DMapView, never settable without edit permission.
  2. Geometry helpers — src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts:
    • wallVertexHandles(level) → { id, wallId, pointIndex, x, y }[] for the active level.
    • previousFloorInBuilding(canvasData, activeLevelId) → nearest lower floor inside the same building group (the snap task consumes it; land it here with its test).
    • Pure functions, tests in src/lib/map/__tests__/wall-vertex-edit.test.ts.
  3. Overlay — src/components/editor/map-wall-edit/MapWallVertexHandles.tsx. Project each handle through computeCoordSpace + makeLevelPixelTransform + pixelToLngLat + levelBaseHeights like MapObjectMarkers does, reposition on render/move/zoom/pitch/rotate, hide handles that are off-screen or not projectable, compact draggable buttons with real hover/focus/drag states.
  4. Write path — drag → lngLatToLevelPixel → replace that one points[pointIndex] → setCanvasDataSilent; on pointerup, setCanvasData once.
  5. Toolbar — toggle in EditorBottomToolbar.tsx inside the existing canEdit block. Title Edit wall points, aria-pressed reflects the mode, mutually exclusive with mapMoveMode (Drag building) in both directions, and visually separate from the placement group (MapScopeButton / MapTransformButton) so it never reads as a placement tool.

Decide these on purpose, not by accident

  1. WallLayer.points is a polyline (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:41-52), not always two points. Handle every vertex by its index — the PRD's "endpoint" is only the 2-point case.
  2. Curved walls carry h1x/h1y/h2x/h2y. Moving a vertex leaves the bezier handles pointing at the old position. PRD non-goal 3 rules out curve editing, so hide handles on walls that have curve handles set rather than silently deforming them.
  3. Only the dragged vertex moves even when another wall ends on the same coordinate (R10): match on wall id + point index, never on coordinate.
  4. Wall geometry is editor data, not placement. The drag must leave level.mapTransform, building.mapTransform and the project offset untouched.

Acceptance

  • Toggle shows only in Editor Map mode and only for useEditorCapabilities().canEdit; viewers see neither the toggle nor handles
  • Mode on → handles on the active floor's wall vertices only; lower floors stay visible but reference-only
  • Mode off → handles gone, and selection, object markers, labels, building drag and placement tools behave exactly as today
  • A drag updates canvasData.levels[].layout.walls[].points live, and the moved point is there after switching to the 2D Editor
  • One completed drag = one undo entry; Undo restores the pre-drag position and does not step through drag frames
  • A press on a handle never starts a map pan, a building drag, or a feature selection
  • A wall sharing that coordinate does not move
  • Floor, building and project transforms are unchanged after a drag
  • Active floor with no walls → no handles, existing message still shown
  • Switching floor clears drag state; a map style reload reattaches and reprojects handles
  • Unit tests: handle extraction, previous-floor resolution, single-vertex move
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

issues.display_title: Issue #689: Editor Map: snap wall vertex drags to the previous floor, with an override key (PRD #681)
issues.main_description_html:
While a wall vertex is dragged in Map mode, it should snap to the floor below — that is the whole point of correcting geometry in the 3D view instead of the 2D Editor — with a key to drag freely when the target genuinely is not on the floor below.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From PRD #681 — R15–R18. Builds on #688 (the mode, the handles and the drag write path); that one lands previousFloorInBuilding(), this one uses it.

What is already in the repo

  • src/lib/map/floorSnap.ts snaps a floor's footprint bbox to its neighbours — center/min/max per axis (#594). Different problem: it never looks at a vertex, so the geometry here is new. Copy its shape, not its math: pure module, everything passed in, no store/map/DOM reads, so drag and tests cannot drift.
  • src/lib/map/useSnapGuideLayer.ts (SNAP_GUIDE_SOURCE / SNAP_GUIDE_LAYER) already renders snap feedback as a map line and takes matches as input — the feedback surface exists, and Editor3DMapView.tsx:251-259 shows how it is wired.
  • previousFloorInBuilding() in src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts resolves the reference floor; groupLevelsByBuilding() (geojson-utils.ts:860) is what makes it per-building.

Scope

  1. snapWallVertex(point, targets, options) in src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts → snapped point + what it caught (or free).
  2. Target extraction from the previous floor's walls: every vertex, plus the nearest point on each wall segment.
  3. Vertex beats segment when both are in range — a corner is what the user is aiming at.
  4. Alt held (or equivalent) = free drag, no snap, no snap state. Held state read at drag time, not at drag start, so it can be pressed mid-drag.
  5. Snap feedback while snapped: changed dot state, plus a guide/highlight of the caught target.
  6. No previous floor in the building → free drag and no snap affordance at all; the mode still works.

Decide these on purpose

  1. Snap radius unit. Model px is what the geometry is in, but a fixed model-px radius snaps everything at low zoom and nothing at high zoom. Convert a screen-px threshold to model px per drag frame instead, and leave it as a tunable knob.
  2. Snapping is in the active floor's px space. The previous floor has its own mapTransform; its targets must be brought into the dragged floor's space (or both into the building frame, as floorSnap.ts does) before any distance is compared — comparing raw points across two aligned floors silently snaps to the wrong place.
  3. Snap decides the committed value too: whatever snapWallVertex returns is what setCanvasData writes on pointerup, so a snapped release stores the snapped coordinate exactly, not a near-miss.

Acceptance

  • Dragging near a previous-floor wall vertex snaps to it
  • Dragging near a previous-floor wall segment snaps to the nearest point on it
  • A vertex within range wins over a segment within range
  • Holding the override key drags freely, and releasing the drag commits the free position
  • Snap feedback is visible while snapped and gone when not
  • Active floor with no previous floor in its building: free drag, no snap state, no errors
  • The previous floor is never edited or selectable through this
  • Snapping does not change floor, building or project transforms
  • Unit tests: vertex-over-segment priority, radius boundary, snapping disabled = free point returned unchanged, cross-floor mapTransform handled
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green
